name: visual-c
thesis: Elaborate the director-approved 'Forge' character (deep navy/charcoal, crimson/gold/cool-blue, layered depth, controlled motion) into a token/component/state system whose one organising rule is: HUE says which authority family you are in, CONSTRUCTION (fill vs outline vs hatch, hard edge vs soft edge, glyph + word) says the exact state, and MOTION is spent only on transitions and on the single thing that is actually running. The mockup's palette survives almost intact once sampled; what must change for the non-negotiables is small and is listed as departures: crimson is reserved for actions that write to the game, green is reserved for verdicts (not the Validate button), violet/blue/amber lane tints never appear on a pill or banner, illustrated hero/lane art becomes CSS-drawn atmosphere (a userscript bundle cannot fetch it and should not carry 250 KB of JPEG), the brush wordmark becomes a system-font or embedded-vector wordmark, and every status row gets a glyph and a word beside its colour.

user_decisions_surfaced: D-VC-1 Crimson reserved for game-writing actions: the mockup paints 'New Content' (authoring) crimson. Proposal: only LIVE WRITE and its buttons may be crimson-filled; authoring a manifest uses the neutral raised control. Director may keep crimson on 'New Content' only if that action really opens a live-write flow.

D-VC-2 Green reserved for verdicts: the mockup's 'Validate Content' quick action is a green card. Proposal: Validate uses the blue/neutral action treatment; green appears only on VERIFIED/ok verdicts and the session lamp.

D-VC-3 Illustrated hero and lane art: proposal replaces raster illustration with CSS-drawn atmosphere (gradients + 1-2 KB inline SVG noise/glyph) so the bundle stays self-contained and under the 16 MB/perf budget on Android; the director can later supply a repo-committed data-URI art pack behind a 'Rich art' setting (off by default on phone).

D-VC-4 Wordmark: system-font 'FORGE' with crimson hard offset (option A) or an embedded vector path drawn with createElementNS (option B, the only way to keep the brushed lettering). Needs a director pick; A is the recommendation.

D-VC-5 Light theme: proposal ships dark only plus a 'Daylight' high-contrast dark variant (one class, five token overrides). A true light theme doubles the contrast audit and is deferred unless the director wants it.

D-VC-6 PUBLISH confirmation construction: gold seal card + solid gold button + typed record count or 600 ms press-and-hold. This is K-12 territory; proposal shows the construction, the director sets the confirmation level.

D-VC-7 Amber (warn/recovery) vs gold (publish) are 1.11:1 apart in luminance and ~15 degrees in hue; they are separated by construction (dark fill + outline + triangle vs solid seal + diamond). If the director wants a hue separation as well, warn shifts to #f08a3c (more orange) at the phase-2 design freeze.
weaknesses: Two red families (burnt-crimson LIVE WRITE fill vs coral FAILED text) and two yellow families (gold PUBLISH seal vs amber WARN/RECOVERY) are deliberately close in hue; they are told apart by construction and by word/glyph, not by colour. This is correct for colour-blind safety but means a reviewer skimming only colours could conflate them; the construction rules must be enforced by a stylesheet contract test, not by taste.

Hard-edged ink controls (radius 0, offset shadow) used beside soft 8 px cards can look inconsistent if applied too widely; the proposal limits them to mode chips, risk buttons, pills and the wordmark, and that limit needs a written component inventory to hold.

The CSS-drawn atmosphere (layered radial gradients, thin SVG glyphs) will read as less 'painted' than the mockup's illustrations; the director approved a look that had art in it, so this is a visible departure even though it is the correct one for a self-contained userscript.
The segmented per-item progress bar degrades to a bucketed bar above ~40 items and to a plain fraction above ~120; large batch manifests lose the per-item glance.

Contrast is verified only for the token pairs listed; any ad-hoc rgba() blend added in implementation (glows, scrims over lane art, hover tints) must be re-computed at its composite value, and the 88 % scrim figure assumes a worst-case white pixel beneath it.

The mode header consumes 44 px of a 390x844 viewport while sticky; with the top bar (56) and bottom action bar (64) plus bottom nav (56) that is 220 px of chrome on the run screen. The proposal collapses the bottom nav while a run is open to win 56 px back, which is itself a behaviour the roadmap must test.

Firefox Android support for adoptedStyleSheets, backdrop-filter and prefers-reduced-motion is assumed from platform knowledge, not verified in this session; the fallbacks (insertRule path already in dom.mjs, no backdrop-filter dependency) are designed so nothing state-bearing needs them.
The proposal does not settle IA or destination names; it styles whatever the IA panel recommends inside the approved shell, and the phone bottom-nav treatment assumes five or fewer destinations.

proposal.one_line: The approved dark TNR operations console, tokenised from the mockup's own pixels: navy-charcoal ground, ivory ink, a crimson that only ever means 'this writes to the game', a gold that only ever means 'this publishes', cool blue for the system's resting state, lane tints that are decoration and nothing more, ember-glow reserved for the one thing currently running, and hard-edged ink controls where a decision is being made.
proposal.relationship_to_the_approved_direction: This is not an alternative to the north star; it is the north star made buildable. Every hex below is traced to a sampled region of the approved mockup or is the smallest adjustment needed to pass AA/3:1 or the no-runtime-assets rule. Departures are enumerated in mockup_departures and are each a director-visible decision (user_decisions_surfaced), never silent.

design_tokens.scope_rule: All custom properties are declared on .f-host and .f-app (styles.mjs:19-20 pattern), never on :root; color-scheme: dark stays on those two elements. Lane tokens are additionally declared only inside .f-lane so they cannot leak into pills/banners.

--mut-edge.role: 2 px hard rule on every crimson band/button top+bottom (6.31:1 on bg, 5.19:1 on raised) so the band's boundary never depends on the 2.92:1 fill-vs-paper difference; also the rail's active marker

--mut-glow.role: 8-24 px outer glow allowed ONLY on a crimson button while it is focused/pressed (never resting, never ambient)

--pub.role: PUBLISH: the only solid gold fill (seal card border, Publish button, mode band). Dark text on it 10.00:1

--warn-fill.role: warn banner fill (warn text on it 7.47:1, ink 13.40:1)

--sent-fill.role: SENT pill/banner base (orchid on it 7.73:1, ink 13.35:1)

--bad.from_mockup: no source; a coral, bright and text-weight, so it is the opposite construction of the dark crimson fill (2.91:1 between them in luminance, and never in the same construction)

--focus.role: focus ring: 2 px solid, outline-offset 3 px so it is always drawn on the surrounding dark surface (18.09:1 bg, 16.67:1 paper); on a gold seal the offset is what saves it (ring directly on gold would be 1.78:1)

state_pills.construction: Every pill = [glyph][space][WORD] in 12 px / 700 / uppercase / 0.04 em tracking, min-height 24 px, padding 2 px 8 px, radius 0 (hard edge), 1 px border in the state colour, text in the state colour, on --paper. Glyphs are plain Unicode text nodes (no icon font). Pills never animate and never change size on state change (all glyphs are single-cell).

SENT.note: the only pill with a dashed border, the only pill whose word carries a qualifier, and the only pill with a question glyph; it is 2 px so it is heavier than VERIFIED

CONFIRMED.note: half-disc glyph: landed, not yet read back

VERIFIED.note: the only green pill; the only pill with a solid tinted fill among lifecycle states, so 'decisively finished' reads at a glance

ORPHANED.note: flag glyph + hatch + 2 px: the one amber pill that demands a human decision

SKIPPED.text_decoration: none (strikethrough rejected: hurts legibility at 12 px)

PAUSED.note: job-level; the pause REASON is always printed beside it as a mono chip (SESSION / 429 / NETWORK / AMBIGUOUS / USER / ORPHANED)

INCOMPLETE.note: quarter-disc glyph: finished but owes a read-back; word carries the qualifier so it is never mistaken for DONE

DONE_unverified_or_failed.note: DONE with outcome != success is never rendered as a green pill; it renders as INCOMPLETE-style (amber, unverified) or FAILED-style per jobOutcome() (A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:107)

RUNNING.note: the pill itself is static; the ember sheen lives on the progress track next to it, never on the pill

content_HIDDEN.note: slate fill: present but not player-visible; the default state Forge creates into

content_DRAFT.note: a repo package / staged edit not yet applied to a live record; dashed because it is not live

content_PUBLISHED.note: gold outline: the state that the gold PUBLISH action produces; outline (state) vs solid (action) keeps them apart

contrast_table_text_on_background: #282e35 lane scrim (88 % bg over worst-case white art)
contrast_table_non_text_ui_3to1: FAIL by fill alone -> band always carries 2 px #ff5f5a rules: 6.31 on bg, 5.19 on raised
different enough plus different construction; lane violet never appears on a pill
bright text vs dark fill; never in the same construction
NOT separable by luminance: separated by construction (dark fill+outline+triangle vs solid seal+diamond) and by word; see D-VC-7

typography.ui_family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif  (on Samsung Android/Firefox this resolves to Roboto or Samsung One via system-ui; no @font-face, no fetch)
typography.mono_family: ui-monospace, "Roboto Mono", "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace  (ids, procedure paths, hashes, snapshot keys, raw payloads only; amendment §11)
typography.display: No display face. Brand identity is carried by weight (800-900), tracking and the crimson hard offset, see brand.

scale_phone_390.caption: 12px/16px 600 (pill words, mono ids, budget numbers only)

typography.weights: 400 body, 600 controls/labels, 700 headings and pills, 800-900 brand and mode words. Nothing below 400; no italics except the optional quote in the hero (which carries no state).
typography.line_height: 1.45 body (styles.mjs:19 today), 1.25 headings, 1 for single-line controls/pills
typography.numerals: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on counts, budgets, countdowns so digits do not jitter on the 1.5 s re-render (app.mjs:268)
typography.why_it_reads_at_390_in_daylight: Body is 15 px ivory at 15.12:1 on card; secondary is 13 px at 8.19:1 (double the AA minimum), so a 50 % brightness drop in sun still leaves margin; nothing state-bearing is under 12 px and the 12 px items are 600-700 weight uppercase words with a glyph, which survive glare better than lowercase thin text; the 'Daylight' variant lifts --mute to #c5ccd8 (10.74:1) and --edge to #738399 for outdoor use; line length is capped at ~60 ch by the 358 px card so wrapped error text stays scannable; no text is ever set over raster art (lane titles sit on a solid 88 % scrim: 11.94:1 worst case).

spacing_and_density.touch_targets: 44 px minimum for every tappable thing (unchanged from styles.mjs:31); 48 px for risk buttons (Start job (LIVE), Publish, Reconcile & resume, Adopt); bottom nav items 56 px tall x >= 64 px wide; list rows >= 56 px; pills are not tap targets (rows are)
spacing_and_density.radius: cards 8 px; neutral buttons and inputs 6 px; lane cards 10 px; pills, mode chips, mode bands, risk buttons and the wordmark 0 px (hard edge, ink style); dialogs 10 px; progress track 2 px
spacing_and_density.gaps: 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 px scale; card padding 12 px 14 px on phone, 16 px 18 px on desktop; section gap 16 px phone, 24 px desktop; page gutter 16 px phone, 24 px tablet, 32 px desktop

card_widths.390: one column; card = 358 px (390 - 2x16); lane cards 358 x 96 px as horizontal strips (icon + title + subtitle + chevron), not 200 px tall tiles
card_widths.768: two columns of 352 px with 16 px gap inside a 736 px content area; lanes 3-up at 229 px tiles
card_widths.1280: rail 232 px; content 1008 px at 32 px gutter = 944 px usable; Command Center 12-col grid: quick actions 4-up (224 px), lanes 6-up (146 px) or 3-up x 2 rows (301 px) when the IA settles on six, bottom row 3 columns (301 px); run screen 60/40 split (556 px / 364 px)

spacing_and_density.density_rule: Desktop may show the full item table, budget meters, captures and the journal tail at once; phone shows the verdict, the mode band, the action bar and the item list, with budget/captures/journal behind a 'Technical' details group that is expanded automatically only when it carries a problem (tripped budget, unpersisted capture).

motion.principle: Motion never carries state. Anything that animates is either (a) a spatial transition between two already-rendered states or (b) the single 'running' indicator. State text, pills, banners and counts appear at their final value on the same frame as the DOM update.

durations_and_easing.press: 90 ms, ease-out (translate 2px 2px + shadow 5->3 px on ink buttons, mirroring globals.css:270-289 at pin 345d18ac)
durations_and_easing.card_enter_section_switch: 180 ms ease-out: opacity 0->1 and translateY 6->0 px on the new screen's root; no exit animation (old screen is replaced immediately, dom.mjs replace())
durations_and_easing.details_expand: 220 ms ease-out on max-height/opacity of the details body; the summary word changes instantly
durations_and_easing.progress_width: 300 ms linear on the fill width; the numeric fraction beside it updates instantly
durations_and_easing.lane_glow: 150 ms on box-shadow when a lane card is focused/pressed
durations_and_easing.ember_sheen: 1.6 s linear infinite translateX of a 40 %-wide gradient across the RUNNING progress track only; paused when document.hidden or any dialog is open; removed on DONE/PAUSED/INCOMPLETE

motion.reduced_motion: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) scoped under .f-app: every transition-duration and animation-duration -> 0.01 ms; ember sheen replaced by a static 2 px --acc rule at the track's leading edge; progress width still updates (no transition); details open instantly. Additionally a Settings toggle 'Reduce motion' sets .f-app.rm with the same rules, because the OS preference cannot be assumed to be exposed correctly through a userscript overlay on Firefox Android (unverified).
never_animates: verdict banners (Verified / Finished UNVERIFIED / Finished with failures / Read-only capture complete)
the operation-mode band's colour, label or counts
pause-reason chip and 429 countdown text (updates by text replacement only)
confirm dialogs' content and backdrop (backdrop appears at full opacity; the page beneath freezes: sheen paused)
toasts' text (a toast may fade in 120 ms; its content is final on first paint)
anything on a data table or list row (no row highlight sweeps, no shimmer)
background/hero atmosphere (static gradients; no drift, no particles)
motion.allowed_summary: press feedback, hover/focus colour, screen enter fade-slide, details expand, progress width, lane glow on interaction, one ember sheen on one running track, toast fade-in

status_visualization.job_progress: Segmented track, 12 px tall, 1 px --edge border, radius 2, one cell per item (max 40 cells; 41-120 items -> cells of ceil(n/40) items coloured by the worst state in the bucket; >120 -> plain fraction bar). Cell fills: VERIFIED #5ad48f solid; CONFIRMED #7ab8ff solid; SENT #e79cff hatch; FAILED #ff8a80 solid with a 1 px dark gap either side; SKIPPED #5d6d82; ORPHANED #f5a25a hatch; PLANNED transparent. The cell currently in flight carries the ember sheen. Beneath it, one 13 px line in tabular numerals: '7 verified · 1 SENT unconfirmed · 1 failed · 3 planned · 12 total' with each count in its state colour AND its glyph. Sketch (390): [✓✓✓✓✓✓✓][◐][?///][✕][ ][ ][ ]
status_visualization.per_item_state: Row = [idx] [name 15px] [pill] then a second 13 px line [entity · phase · id in mono]; error text in --bad 13 px wrapped; drift as a details group whose summary is 'drift on N keys' in --warn. SENT rows additionally get a 3 px dashed --sent left rule on the row; ORPHANED rows a 3 px solid --warn left rule; FAILED a 3 px --bad rule. The left rule is a second redundant cue that survives a colour-blind read because it is also a different line style (dashed vs solid).
status_visualization.budget: Per-path meter row: [path in mono 12px] [8 px track, 1 px --edge, fill --acc] [used/allowance in tabular 12px] [resets in mm:ss]. At >= 80 % the fill becomes --warn and the row gains a ▲ glyph before the numbers; TRIPPED renders the track as --bad hatch, the numbers replaced by 'TRIPPED until hh:mm' in --bad with ✕, and the row is expanded out of the Technical group automatically. Nothing spent -> a single --mute line 'nothing spent this minute'.
status_visualization.auth_state: A 'session lamp' chip in the shell (top bar on phone, rail footer on desktop), always visible, never a banner while READY: [✓ SESSION] --ok = READY; [… SESSION] --acc = PROBING; [? SESSION] --warn = UNCONFIRMED (could not confirm; not a read failure); [✕ SESSION] --bad = SIGNED_OUT/refused. The three failure-ish states keep distinct glyphs and words so 'unavailable', 'denied' and 'transport failed' (amendment §9) never collapse into one red lamp; a NETWORK pause is a separate --warn chip [✗ NETWORK] on the job, not on the lamp. When not READY, the full explanatory banner of app.mjs:143-150 still renders on the screen that needs it (manifest preflight, run), with the Re-check button.
status_visualization.publish_state: Content rows carry the content pill (HIDDEN slate / DRAFT dashed blue / PUBLISHED gold outline). A publish action renders as a 'seal' card: 2 px solid --pub border, a second inner 1 px --pub rule at 4 px inset (double rule), ◆ PUBLISH in --pub-text 14 px/900 at the top, the record name, the exact flip in words ('hidden: true → false on item 7c3…'), a dependency line (referenced records still hidden, in --warn with ▲), and one solid gold hard-edged button 'Publish 1 record → LIVE' with --pub-ink text and a 5 px 5 px 0 #1b1200 offset shadow. After read-back the seal card's header becomes '✓ PUBLISHED · read back' in --ok; if read-back is unread it becomes '◔ PUBLISH SENT · UNVERIFIED' in --warn and the row's pill stays HIDDEN with a '?' until verified.
status_visualization.capture_persistence: 'N captures' vs 'N full captures' keep separate wording (screens.mjs:104-112) and additionally a full capture shows a ▣ glyph and the word FULL in --warn before the path, plus the sentence about repository persistence; summary captures show ▢ SUMMARY in --mute. 'body persisted' = ✓ in --ok; 'not persisted' = ✕ in --bad.
status_visualization.recent_activity: Rows use the real state pill of the underlying job/record, never a free-coloured dot (mockup departure #6).

risk_states.today_baseline: Live and read-only starts share one button style (.f-primary = --acc fill, styles.mjs:33; screens.mjs:151-156) and differ only in the window.confirm sentence (app.mjs:172-175). SENT is a 999 px-radius outline pill in --sent #b08cff that is the same construction as CONFIRMED (styles.mjs:43). ORPHANED, PAUSED and INCOMPLETE share --warn (styles.mjs:45). An open job is a generic .f-banner.warn (screens.mjs:18-26) and 'Reconcile & resume' is the same blue .f-primary as any other primary (screens.mjs:24,225). Publish does not exist (A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:151). The auth banner is a full-width .f-banner on every screen (app.mjs:132-151).
risk_states.live_mutation_screen: Above the manifest's item list and pinned (sticky, below the top bar) sits the LIVE WRITE band: --mut fill, 2 px --mut-edge rules top and bottom, radius 0, 44 px tall, containing '⚠ LIVE WRITE' in 14 px/900 --mut-ink, then count chips on --raised: '3 CREATES', '2 UPDATES', '1 UPLOAD', '0 PUBLISHES' in tabular 800. The Start button is the only crimson-filled control: hard edge, 48 px, --mut fill, --mut-ink text 'Start job → writes 5 records', 5 px 5 px 0 #5a0d13 offset shadow, and on focus/press an 0 0 20 px --mut-glow. Read-only manifests get the READ ONLY band in --read-fill with '◉ READ ONLY · 0 writes' and a blue --acc primary button 'Run captures'; the two cannot be confused at arm's length: different band colour, different words, different button fill, different glyph. The confirm dialog restates the band's counts and is drawn on --float with the page frozen (sheen paused, no motion behind it).
risk_states.publish_action: The PUBLISH band (solid --pub fill, --pub-ink text '◆ PUBLISH · 1 record → player-visible', hard edge) replaces the LIVE WRITE band on publish flows, so gold on the screen always means 'this makes content visible to players'. The seal card and gold button are described under status_visualization.publish_state. Confirmation construction: typed count or press-and-hold (director decision D-VC-6 / K-12). The Content Admin list row for 'Publish / Unpublish' is NOT a plain chevron row (mockup departure #4): it is rendered as a gold-outlined hard-edged row with the ◆ glyph and the pending count, visually heavier than Preview/Edit.
risk_states.ambiguous_SENT: Job level: a SENT banner in the SENT construction (hatched --sent-fill, 2 px dashed --sent border, '? 1 WRITE UNCONFIRMED' in 14 px/900 --sent) sits directly under the RECOVERY band with the sentence 'The request left this device and no answer was recorded. Nothing is retried; Reconcile reads the server first.' The only primary on the screen is 'Reconcile & resume' in the RECOVERY construction (amber hard-edged outline button with ‖ glyph and 2 px --warn border), never a blue or green fill. Item level: the SENT pill (dashed, hatched, qualifier word) plus the dashed left rule on the row. There is no button anywhere on a SENT item whose label is 'Retry' or 'Send again'; the Re-send option that exists today for an update-phase orphan (screens.mjs:66) is rendered as a --bad-outlined hard-edged button labelled 'Re-send update (I have checked the record)' with ⚠, positioned last.
risk_states.paused_or_orphaned_job: The RECOVERY band (hatched --rec-fill, 2 px --warn rules, '‖ RECOVERY' + counts 'SENT 1 · ORPHANED 2 · PLANNED 4') is pinned on the run screen and, on the Command Center, the resumable job card carries the same band as its header instead of today's generic warn banner. The pause reason is a mono chip beside the PAUSED pill: 'SESSION' with ✕ in --bad (and the Resume button disabled with the reason text, app.mjs:159-163 preserved), '429' with ▲ in --warn and a live countdown in tabular numerals, 'NETWORK' ✗ --warn, 'AMBIGUOUS' ? --sent, 'USER' ‖ --mute, 'ORPHANED' ⚑ --warn. Orphan cards: 2 px solid --warn hard border, hatched 8 px corner tab reading DECIDE, candidates as rows with 'Adopt <id>' as a --warn-outlined ink button, 'Skip (leave as is)' as a neutral button with the existing sentence, and the card never shows a green or blue primary.
risk_states.why_more_obvious_than_today: Today: one hue difference on a 12 px pill and one sentence in window.confirm. Proposed: a 44 px pinned band whose colour, glyph and word differ per mode; a button whose fill differs per mode; a pill whose border style, fill texture, glyph and word differ per state; a row rule whose line style differs per state; and a rule that green and blue fills cannot appear on a screen in RECOVERY or on any SENT item.

light_dark.default: Dark only. The approved character is dark and atmospheric (amendment §2-3); the mockup has no light state.
light_dark.daylight_variant: A second dark variant, not a light theme: .f-app.f-daylight overrides --mute #c5ccd8 (10.74:1 on paper), --dim #a3afc1 (7.81:1), --edge #738399 (4.49:1), --line #3a4757, and raises pill borders to 2 px. Toggle in Settings, remembered in localStorage next to the existing settings keys. Cost: ~6 declarations.
light_dark.light_theme: Deferred (D-VC-5). If wanted later: mechanism is the same as today, tokens on .f-host/.f-app (styles.mjs:19-20) with a .f-light class override and color-scheme: light; every pair in the contrast table must be recomputed; the crimson/gold/blue accents would need darker text-grade variants (#9a1b25, #8a6a12, #1f5fbf) because the current ones are tuned for dark ground.
light_dark.system_preference: prefers-color-scheme is deliberately ignored: the overlay sits on the game page and must not flip its look because the OS is in light mode.

allowed: three elevation levels with real shadows: paper 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.4); raised 0 4px 14px rgba(0,0,0,.45); float 0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.55) plus 1 px --edge2

static atmosphere: on .f-bg a layered radial-gradient (crimson ember at 8 % alpha bottom-left, cool blue at 6 % top-right) over --bg, plus an optional 1 KB inline-SVG grain at 4 % alpha; hero region of the Command Center may add a 2 KB inline-SVG silhouette (torii/roofline) at 10 % alpha, drawn with createElementNS
lane cards: gradient wash in the lane tint (20 % -> 0 %) over --paper, a lane glyph at 12 % alpha, 1 px tint edge, and on focus/press a 0 0 0 1px tint + 0 0 24px tint@35 % glow
ember sheen on the single running progress track
ink offset shadows on hard-edged controls (5 px 5 px 0, colour = a darker step of the control's own family)
screen enter fade-slide 180 ms; details expand 220 ms; press translate 2 px
the wordmark's crimson slash/offset and a thin crimson rule under the top bar
banned: any animation that runs while nothing is running (ambient drift, particles, aurora, animated gradients, glow breathing)
shimmer/skeleton loops beyond 2 cycles; skeletons are static blocks after that
motion on pills, banners, mode bands, counts, lamps, orphan cards, dialogs
glow on danger/warn/bad elements (glow = 'active', never = 'danger'; danger is hard-edged and still)
raster imagery fetched at runtime or embedded above ~8 KB total; text over any image without a solid >= 88 % scrim
lane tints on pills, banners, buttons, progress cells or the mode band
green fills on buttons; crimson fills outside LIVE WRITE; gold fills outside PUBLISH
transparency/blur (backdrop-filter) as a load-bearing separation cue; it is decorative only and must degrade to a solid --raised on Firefox Android
flashiness_budget.measurement: The stylesheet contract test lists every selector allowed to declare animation/transition and every selector allowed to use --mut, --pub, --ok as background; a new selector outside the list fails the build, the same way innerHTML fails it today (forge/build.mjs per A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:163).

implementation_cost.today: forge/src/ui/styles.mjs = 6,197 bytes, ~60 rules, one TOKENS string, no media queries, no animation (grep finds none).
implementation_cost.proposed: ~16-20 KB unminified (~4.5-5.5 KB gzip) in one stylesheet: ~70 tokens, ~150 rules, 2 media queries (min-width 768, 1280), 1 prefers-reduced-motion block, 1 .f-daylight block, 1 keyframes (sheen), 4 hatch gradients, ~12 elevation/glow declarations. Inline SVG atmosphere adds ~3 KB of createElementNS code. Total UI delta ~+15 KB on a 398 KB bundle (A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:171), i.e. under 4 %.
implementation_cost.code_changes: pill() (screens.mjs:8) becomes pill(state, {glyph, word}) reading a STATE table; a ModeBand(app, mode, counts) component; a SessionLamp; a SegmentedProgress; Banner gains a construction class (fill/outline/hatch); buttons gain .f-ink (hard edge) and .f-mut/.f-pub/.f-rec variants. All createElement + CSSOM (dom.mjs:3-16,30-43); no new dependency.
implementation_cost.gates: a stylesheet contract test that (1) parses the CSS text, (2) asserts every selector is scoped under .f-host/.f-app/.f-boot, (3) asserts animation/transition appear only on the allow-listed selectors, (4) asserts --mut/--pub/--ok backgrounds appear only on allow-listed selectors, (5) recomputes the contrast table from the TOKENS string with the same formula as palette_c.py and fails under 4.5:1 for text pairs and 3:1 for edge pairs.

what_it_borrows_from_the_game.ink_button_mechanics: globals.css:243-296 at pin 345d18ac: radius 0, 2 px border, offset box-shadow (5 px 5 px 0), hover translate 2 px with shadow 3 px, 150 ms transitions, focus outline 2 px ivory offset 4 px. Borrowed as the .f-ink construction for mode chips and risk buttons only. The game applies it as a special class beside ordinary rounded-md shadow-sm buttons (button.tsx:16-36), which is exactly the 'selective' use the amendment asks for.
what_it_borrows_from_the_game.ivory_and_crimson: The game's ink primary is ivory #f8f1dc on a #26110c border with a #b7331f offset; this proposal's --ink2 #fffaf0 and crimson family are the same idea shifted onto a navy ground.
what_it_borrows_from_the_game.dark_palette_family: The game's dark scheme is hsl(222 47% 11%) background / hsl(217 33% 17%) card (globals.css:138-142), i.e. navy-charcoal; --bg #0b121a and --paper #121b26 sit in the same hue family so the overlay reads as belonging to the game without copying its chrome.
what_it_borrows_from_the_game.not_borrowed: No game fonts, icons, images, page chrome, parchment page backgrounds, or the game's light theme. No franchise references.

rejected_alternatives: Crimson as text (mockup's red 'TNR' lettering and red nav edge as text colours): #cd1c24 on the ground is 3.2:1; rejected for any text; crimson is fill-only with ivory on it.
Pure white text (mockup): passes contrast but the amendment asks for warm ivory and white glares more on an AMOLED phone; ivory at 16.4:1 loses nothing.

Rounded 999 px pills (today, styles.mjs:42): rejected in favour of hard-edged pills so the pill family visibly belongs to the ink system and so dashed/2 px borders read clearly at 12 px (dashes render poorly on a 999 px radius).
Separate hue for READ ONLY (cyan) distinct from --acc: rejected; a fourth cool hue adds nothing a word and glyph do not, and the safe mode should look like the system's default.
Distinct hue for RECOVERY (e.g. orange-red): rejected; recovery is caution, not failure and not success; sharing the amber family with a hatched construction says exactly that.
Keeping violet for SENT at today's #b08cff: rejected because the Characters lane in the mockup is violet; SENT moves to orchid #e79cff and lanes may never colour a pill.
Green quick-action card for Validate (mockup): rejected; green is a verdict colour only.

Embedding the mockup's illustrations as data URIs: rejected for v1 (249 KB JPEG at 1536 px, larger than the whole UI layer; would be parsed on every game page the loader matches); CSS atmosphere instead, art pack as an opt-in later.
A true light theme in v1: deferred, see light_dark.
Count-up number animation on the mode band: rejected; counts are state.
Toast-only outcome reporting (today's app.mjs:295): kept as a secondary echo only; the verdict banner on the run screen is the primary surface and is static.

accessibility.focus: 2 px solid --focus (#fffaf0) outline, outline-offset 3 px on every interactive element under .f-app; on hard-edged ink buttons the offset ring sits outside the offset shadow. Verified 18.09:1 on bg, 16.67:1 on paper; the offset is mandatory because the ring on gold would be 1.78:1. :focus-visible only, so touch taps do not leave rings.
accessibility.colour_blind_redundancy: Every state = colour + word + glyph + construction: PLANNED ○ dotted; SENT ? dashed+hatch+qualifier; CONFIRMED ◐ solid thin; VERIFIED ✓ solid+fill; FAILED ✕ solid thick; ORPHANED ⚑ thick+hatch+qualifier; SKIPPED →| neutral; PAUSED ‖; INCOMPLETE ◔+qualifier; HIDDEN ◌ slate fill; DRAFT ✎ dashed; PUBLISHED ◆ gold outline. Modes = glyph + word + fill/hatch: ◉ READ ONLY (blue fill), ⚠ LIVE WRITE (crimson fill + edge rules), ◆ PUBLISH (gold fill), ‖ RECOVERY (amber hatch). Session lamp = glyph + word. Under a deuteranopia simulation the pairs that collapse in hue (warn/pub, ok/acc, sent/lane-violet) remain distinct by fill-vs-outline, hatch, border style and word.
accessibility.aria: pills are <span role='status'> only where they change during a run (job pill, running item); the mode band is <header aria-live='polite'> with the counts; the verdict banner is role='alert' when it appears; progress track is role='progressbar' with aria-valuenow/max and an aria-label carrying the count sentence; details/summary native; buttons are real <button>s (dom.mjs h() sets attributes, so aria-* passes straight through).
accessibility.touch_and_keyboard: 44/48 px targets; no hover-only affordances (UI_UX_REVIEWER.md:34); Escape closes dialogs; Enter/Space on rows opens the run; tab order = visual order because the DOM is built in visual order.
accessibility.text_sizing: -webkit-text-size-adjust stays 100 % on the entry splash only (styles.mjs:15); inside the overlay, rem is not used because the carrier page's root font size is the game's; all sizes are px on .f-app so a game stylesheet cannot resize Forge text (scoping rule, styles.mjs:1-9).
accessibility.language: Labels use words that state consequence: 'writes 5 records', 'player-visible', 'unconfirmed', 'nothing is retried'. The mode band never uses 'safe'; it states the mode and the counts.

brand.wordmark_option_A_recommended: 'FORGE' set in the system UI face at 900 weight, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.14em, --ink2, with a 2 px 2 px 0 crimson (#c0242f) text-shadow on phone and 3 px 3 px 0 on desktop (the ink-button offset applied to type), preceded by a 4 px-wide crimson slash drawn as a skewed <span> (transform: skewX(-18deg), background --mut). 'TNR' sits above it at 11 px/800 0.20em --mute on desktop; on phone the two words compress to 'TNR FORGE' on one line. Zero bytes of assets.
brand.wordmark_option_B: An embedded vector: a single <svg><path> built with createElementNS from a ~1.5 KB path string constant, filled --ink2 with a crimson offset copy behind it, giving the mockup's brushed 'FORGE' silhouette. Still no fetch. Costs a designer's path once and a director check that the shape carries no proprietary identity.
brand.phone_top_bar: 56 px bar: slash + 'FORGE' at 15 px/900 (option A) or the SVG at 20 px tall (option B), left-aligned; session lamp; Close. The tagline is not shown on phone.
brand.desktop_rail: Rail header 96 px: 'TNR' small over 'FORGE' 24 px/900 with the crimson offset, tagline 'CREATE · VALIDATE · DEPLOY' 11 px/700 0.18em --mute beneath (mockup's tagline, static, carries no state). A 1 px crimson rule under the header. The version string stays in the rail footer next to the session lamp.
brand.brand_colour_rule: Crimson in the brand is a 2-4 px accent (slash, offset, rule), never a fill larger than the wordmark's offset, so the brand cannot be mistaken for a LIVE WRITE band; the band is the only crimson block taller than 4 px.

lane_accents.policy: Lane tints are decoration. They are declared inside .f-lane only, may colour a lane card's gradient wash, its 1 px edge, its glyph and its interaction glow, and nothing else. A lane card carries no lifecycle state; the work inside a lane shows state through the standard pills and bands, whose colours are global tokens and therefore win by construction (no lane selector can reach a .f-pill).

Combat (illustrative name).glyph: ⚔ or a CSS-drawn blade at 12 % alpha
Combat (illustrative name).texture: gradient wash 20 % -> 0 % from the top-left; no raster

lane_accents.image_texture_policy: v1 ships CSS gradients plus at most one inline-SVG glyph per lane (createElementNS, <= 400 bytes each). An optional 'Rich art' setting may later load a repository-committed data-URI pack, off by default on phone; any art sits under a solid 88 % --bg scrim wherever text is drawn (11.94:1 worst case).
lane_accents.lane_card_vs_status_card: Lane card: 10 px radius, tint edge, tint wash, glyph, title 15 px/700 ivory, subtitle 13 px --mute, chevron; glow on interaction; never a pill, never a count in a state colour (a count of hidden records inside a lane is shown as a slate HIDDEN pill, which is a global token). Status card: 8 px radius, --edge boundary, no wash, no glow ever, carries pills/bands/lamps; hard-edged inner elements. The two cannot be confused: one has colour and glow and no state; the other has state and no glow.

READ ONLY.counts: reads N · captures N (FULL n) · writes 0
READ ONLY.contrast: acc on fill 6.47:1; ink on fill 11.69:1

LIVE WRITE.counts: creates N · updates N · uploads N · reads N

PUBLISH.rules: 2px #1b1200 top and bottom (dark rules on gold, 10.00:1)
PUBLISH.counts: publishes N · unpublishes N · records read back N

RECOVERY.counts: SENT N · ORPHANED N · planned N · verified N
RECOVERY.contrast: warn on hatch 5.98:1; ink on hatch >= 13:1

operation_mode_header.geometry: Full content width, 44 px tall on phone and desktop, radius 0, sticky directly beneath the top bar (phone) or at the top of the content column (desktop). Word at left: glyph + MODE in 14 px/900 uppercase 0.08 em. Counts at right as chips on --raised (phone: the two most consequential counts, the rest behind a tap that expands the band to 2 lines; desktop: all counts). The band never animates, never changes height between modes, and is rendered before any item list so it is the first thing read.
operation_mode_header.where_it_appears: Manifest preflight (from the parsed plan: creates/updates/uploads/captures, before Start), run screen (live counts from the journal), publish flow (from the admin action), any job in PAUSED/INCOMPLETE/with SENT or ORPHANED items (RECOVERY, computed from item states A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:93-103). Command Center shows a 28 px mini-chip version on the Active-work card. Screens with no production consequence (Settings, Captures library) show no band rather than a 'safe' band, so the band's presence itself means 'this screen can touch or has touched production'.
operation_mode_header.phone_390: [⚠ LIVE WRITE            3 CREATES  2 UPDATES ▾]  (44 px; tapping ▾ expands to a second 32 px line with uploads/reads)
operation_mode_header.desktop_1280: [⚠ LIVE WRITE   creates 3 · updates 2 · uploads 1 · reads 6 · publishes 0]
operation_mode_header.counts_semantics: Counts come from the plan (preflight) or the journal (run) and are labelled with the amendment §8 vocabulary: records read, records changed (creates + updates), creates, uploads, captures (with FULL n), publishes/unpublishes, deletes (always 0 and shown only if a future authorized workflow adds them).
